interactions.summary: Jiang makes the wordplay case that artificial intelligence is inherently alchemical, and a student connects that claim to a larger course warning about manipulating reality as if humans could replace divinity.

Students extend the analogy to artificial insemination and genetic engineering, and Jiang answers an AI skepticism objection by saying Dante would judge the intent to create God or immortality rather than the current technical success.

claims.claim: Jiang says the phrase 'artificial intelligence' is itself enough to identify AI as alchemy because it names the artificial making of intelligence.
Jiang says the contemporary world assumes there are no moral laws at work and behaves as though humans can become their own God in a post-truth condition.
Jiang agrees that artificial insemination and genetic manipulation aimed at producing perfect offspring also count as alchemy.
Jiang answers the objection that current AI is only a tool by saying Dante would focus on intention: Silicon Valley is trying to create God or immortality even if it never succeeds.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang collapses the whole debate into a single phrase: artificial intelligence means trying to make intelligence the way alchemists tried to make gold.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the lecture's bluntest bridge between Dante and the current technological moment.

signature_moments.moment: The decisive sin is not success but aspiration: people are trying to create God and buy immortality.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns Dante's category from a technical question into a moral one about will.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's key criterion for modern alchemy: the will to exceed created limits matters even before success arrives.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-24 Jiang explicitly diagnoses the present as post-truth and connects AI and Silicon Valley immortality projects to Dante's alchemy problem.
